bundledNote: there’s no separate processing rate to audit — the platform sets it. Savings come from comparing the effective rate against interchange-plus, not from renegotiating a markup.
singleTerminalRisk: ⚠️ One terminal is a single point of failure — if it dies mid-rush, you can’t take cards until it’s replaced. Keep a spare; redundancy beats saving ~$35/mo.

retail.note: On retail net margins of 8–15%, processing can consume up to a third of net profit.

restaurant.note: The average full-service restaurant margin is 2.8% — processing can cost more than the profit it leaves behind.

qsr.note: High volume + low tickets: the fixed per-transaction fee bites hardest here.

hotel.note: Canadian card-accepting businesses routinely surrender 2.5–3.5% of gross sales to processing.

grocery.note: Enormous card volume on thin margins — every basis point is magnified.

salon.note: Card-on-file bookings skew toward the high end of the band.

other.note: A mixed bag by design — compare against your own statements, not a sector average. Card-not-present sales (online, invoiced) price higher than in-person taps.

infraWarns.drops: ⚠️ Wired devices each need a cable run. Without these, there's no wire from the device back to the switch.
infraWarns.ap: ⚠️ With guest Wi-Fi on, skipping access points means no customer coverage.
infraWarns.switch: ⚠️ Without a switch, your wired devices and access points have nothing to plug into.

ubereats.src: Plan structure official (merchants.ubereats.com/ca/en/pricing); tier % reported via Deliverect CA / Avanto Eats / iOrders — accessed 2026-09-28. (Mar 2026 Lite–20% hike was US-only.)

skip.label: SkipTheDishes
skip.src: No official public rates — per-contract. 20–30% reported (Deliverect, Avanto Eats 2026) — accessed 2026-09-28; confirm with your Skip rep

supportGuide.none: No support — you buy a replacement out of pocket when it dies. Cheapest if nothing breaks; most expensive Tuesday when it does.
supportGuide.contract: Monthly contract, tech on site — suits multi-lane or high-volume shops where an hour of downtime costs more than the contract. You call, they come.
supportGuide.breakfix: Pay per visit — suits a single-location owner-operator who can swap a spare off the shelf and wait a day. Fewer moving parts, no monthly bill.
supportGuide.hybrid: Lighter contract + per-visit rate — the middle ground: cheap cover for the big failures, pay-as-you-go for the small stuff.
